Data: "Iron-sensitive RNA regulation by poly C binding proteins" (PMID 41036621),
two GEO series of K562 short-read RNA-seq (polyA, paired-end 150), three
biological replicates per condition, quantified with Salmon (v1.10.2) against
GENCODE v43:

- [GSE279951](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE279951)
  [P1KD]: shRNA against luciferase (`shCtrl`) or PCBP1 (`shPCBP1`).
- [GSE279949](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE279949)
  [chelator]: DMSO (control) or iron chelator 21H7 (`CHEL`), overnight.

The two DTU comparisons at a glance. In each contrast the first term is the
test group and the subtracted one the reference; the test group is the
condition with more PCBP1 activity, so it is the up side for splicelogic.

| | PCBP1 knockdown (GSE279951) | Iron chelation (GSE279949) |
|---|---|---|
| Contrast | `WT_vs_KD = conditionWT - conditionKD` | `CHEL_vs_DMSO = conditionCHEL - conditionDMSO` |
| Test group (up) | `WT` (shCtrl) | `CHEL` (21H7) |
| Reference (down) | `KD` (shPCBP1) | `DMSO` |
| Positive estimate | transcript used more in WT | transcript used more after chelation |
| IE event | exon in WT transcripts, lost after KD | exon in chelated transcripts, absent from DMSO ones |
| FDR filter | `regular_FDR < 0.1` | `regular_FDR < 0.1` |


```{r fold_setup, include=FALSE}
# fold the code of the setup chunks, up to the event counts
knitr::opts_chunk$set(class.source = "fold-hide")
```

```{r libraries, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tibble)

# then load it with devtools (install.packages("devtools") if needed)
devtools::load_all(here("../splicelogic"))
```

# Data

Shared by both comparisons: the downloads, the `SummarizedExperiment` with all
12 samples, and the GENCODE v43 TxDb and exons the DTU results are mapped onto.

## Download data

GEO bundles one Salmon `quant.sf` per sample into a `RAW.tar` per series
(~21MB each). They are extracted into `workflows/data/PCBP1/<GSE>/`.

GEO has only the `quant.sf` files, but tximeta also needs the Salmon
`aux_info/meta_info.json` (it identifies the transcriptome from the index hash
stored there). The authors' `meta_info.json` is not on GEO: place it at
`workflows/data/PCBP1/meta_info.json` and it is copied into an `aux_info/`
folder next to the quant files of each series (same Salmon index for both).

```{r download_data, eval=FALSE}
options(timeout = 600)
geo_dir <- here("workflows/data/PCBP1")
for (gse in c("GSE279949", "GSE279951")) {
  dest <- file.path(geo_dir, gse)
  dir.create(dest, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  tar_file <- file.path(dest, paste0(gse, "_RAW.tar"))
  download.file(
    paste0("https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE279nnn/", gse,
           "/suppl/", gse, "_RAW.tar"),
    tar_file, mode = "wb"
  )
  untar(tar_file, exdir = dest)
  file.remove(tar_file)
  dir.create(file.path(dest, "aux_info"), showWarnings = FALSE)
  file.copy(file.path(geo_dir, "meta_info.json"), file.path(dest, "aux_info"))
}
list.files(geo_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r txdb, eval=FALSE}
library(txdbmaker)
# load TxDb for GRanges conversion
# the quant.sf files use GENCODE v43 transcript IDs (with version), so build the
# TxDb from the same release: the v48 TxDb would drop transcripts whose version changed
# download once (warning: ~50MB compressed, slow from EBI)
gtf <- here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.annotation.gtf.gz")
# curl with -C - resumes a partial file (EBI often times out mid-transfer);
# --retry re-attempts on failure instead of restarting from zero
system2("curl", c("-C", "-", "-L", "--retry", "5", "--retry-delay", "5",
                  "-o", shQuote(gtf),
                  "https://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/databases/gencode/Gencode_human/release_43/gencode.v43.annotation.gtf.gz"))

txdb <- txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF(gtf, format = "gtf")
# GENCODE v43 has ~252k transcripts; far fewer means the GTF download was cut short
length(AnnotationDbi::keys(txdb, "TXNAME"))
# save to not rebuild every time
AnnotationDbi::saveDb(txdb, here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.sqlite"))
```

## Build the SummarizedExperiment

One `SummarizedExperiment` with the 12 samples of both series, imported with
tximeta. The sample table is parsed from the file names,
`<GSM>_<group>_<replicate>_quant.sf.txt.gz`.

```{r make_se, eval=FALSE}
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.sqlite"))
tx2gene <- AnnotationDbi::select(txdb, keys(txdb, "TXNAME"), "GENEID", "TXNAME")

coldata <- data.frame(
  files = list.files(here("workflows/data/PCBP1"),
                     pattern = "_quant\\.sf\\.txt\\.gz$",
                     recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    series = basename(dirname(files)),
    geo_accession = sub("_.*", "", basename(files)),
    group = sub("^GSM[0-9]+_(.+)_[0-9]+_quant.*", "\\1", basename(files)),
    replicate = sub(".*_([0-9]+)_quant.*", "\\1", basename(files)),
    names = paste(group, replicate, sep = "_"),
    experiment = dplyr::case_when(
      series == "GSE279951" ~ "PCBP1_KD",
      series == "GSE279949" ~ "chelator"
    ),
    condition = dplyr::case_when(
      group == "shCtrl" ~ "WT",
      group == "shPCBP1" ~ "KD",
      group == "DMSO" ~ "DMSO",
      group == "CHEL" ~ "CHEL"
    )
  )
coldata

# check how many transcripts in the quant files are in txdb (should be 1;
# tximeta below fails if any are missing)
read.delim(coldata$files[1])$Name %in% tx2gene$TXNAME |> mean()

# tximeta matches the index hash in aux_info/meta_info.json to GENCODE v43, then
# looks in its BiocFileCache for a TxDb named after the v43 GTF: register the
# TxDb built above under that name, so tximeta loads it instead of downloading
# and building its own
bfc <- BiocFileCache::BiocFileCache(tximeta:::getBFCLoc(), ask = FALSE)
in_cache <- BiocFileCache::bfcquery(
  bfc, "gencode.v43.annotation.gtf.gz", field = "rname", exact = TRUE
)
if (nrow(in_cache) == 0) {
  BiocFileCache::bfcadd(
    bfc, rname = "gencode.v43.annotation.gtf.gz",
    fpath = here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.sqlite"), action = "asis"
  )
}

# transcript-level counts; dtuScaledTPM scales TPM by the median transcript
# length of each gene, the tximport setting recommended for DTU
se <- tximeta::tximeta(
  coldata, countsFromAbundance = "dtuScaledTPM", tx2gene = tx2gene
)

se

saveRDS(se, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/PCBP1_SummarizedExperiment.rds"))
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
se <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/PCBP1/PCBP1_SummarizedExperiment.rds"))
dim(se)
colData(se)
```

## Exons for splicelogic

```{r make_exons, eval=FALSE}
# build exon GRangesList and rename from internal TXID to TXNAME
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.sqlite"))
exons <- exonsBy(txdb, by = "tx")
txps <- AnnotationDbi::select(txdb, keys(txdb, "TXID"), c("TXNAME", "GENEID"), "TXID") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(TXID = as.character(TXID))
# rename exons to match tx_name in se, matching by TXID
all.equal(names(exons), txps$TXID)
names(exons) <- txps$TXNAME[match(names(exons), txps$TXID)]
saveRDS(exons, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/gencode.v43.exons.rds"))
```

```{r input_formatting}
# load from saved sqlite
txdb <- AnnotationDbi::loadDb(here("workflows/data/gencode.v43.sqlite"))
# load exons from saved rds
exons <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/PCBP1/gencode.v43.exons.rds"))
```

# PCBP1 knockdown (GSE279951)

## DTU testing with satuRn: PCBP1 knockdown (GSE279951)

We compare control shRNA (`WT`) against PCBP1 knockdown (`KD`) using satuRn.
GEO gives no pairing between the replicates of the two conditions, so there is
no blocking term (unlike `donor` in the RBP workflow).

```{r filter_kd}
se_kd <- se[, se$experiment == "PCBP1_KD"]
dim(se_kd)

# counts >= 10 in at least 3 samples (the size of one group)
keep <- rowSums(assay(se_kd) >= 10) >= 3
se_kd <- se_kd[keep, ]
dim(se_kd)
```

```{r dtu_design_kd}
# KD as reference level
colData(se_kd)$condition <- factor(colData(se_kd)$condition, levels = c("KD", "WT"))

# build design from the factor directly (matches satuRn vignette convention)
condition <- colData(se_kd)$condition
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition)

L <- limma::makeContrasts(
  WT_vs_KD = conditionWT - conditionKD,
  levels = design
)
L
```

```{r dtu_fit_kd, message=FALSE}
rowData(se_kd)$isoform_id <- rowData(se_kd)$tx_name
# flatten CharacterList gene_id to plain character
rowData(se_kd)$gene_id <- vapply(rowData(se_kd)$gene_id, `[`, character(1), 1)

se_kd <- se_kd[
  duplicated(rowData(se_kd)$gene_id) |
    duplicated(rowData(se_kd)$gene_id, fromLast = TRUE),
]
dim(se_kd)
se_kd <- satuRn::fitDTU(se_kd, formula = ~0 + condition)
```

```{r dtu_test_kd, message=FALSE}
se_kd <- satuRn::testDTU(
  object = se_kd,
  contrasts = L,
  diagplot1 = TRUE,
  diagplot2 = TRUE
)
```

```{r dtu_results_kd}
gene_ids <- rowData(se_kd)$gene_id

# every tested transcript; `sig_res_kd` below is the significant subset, and the
# non-significant rows are the background pool for slSampleNonEventExons()
dtu_res_kd <- rowData(se_kd)[["fitDTUResult_WT_vs_KD"]] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("tx_name") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(gene_id = gene_ids) |>
  dplyr::select(tx_name, gene_id, estimates, pval, regular_FDR) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pval)

sig_res_kd <- dtu_res_kd |> dplyr::filter(regular_FDR < 0.1)

sig_res_kd <- sig_res_kd |> mutate(tx_id = tx_name)
sig_res_kd
# save for later use
saveRDS(dtu_res_kd, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/dtu_res_kd.rds"))
saveRDS(sig_res_kd, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/sig_res_kd.rds"))
```

```{r load_sig_res_kd}
# load the saved DTU results
sig_res_kd <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/PCBP1/sig_res_kd.rds"))
sig_res_kd
```

## Splice event detection with splicelogic for PCBP1 knockdown

We run event detection on the PCBP1 knockdown comparison (`sig_res_kd`); the
chelator comparison gets the same steps in its own section below.

### Direction of the events

WT (PCBP1 present) is the up side and KD (no PCBP1) the reference. In the
contrast `WT_vs_KD = conditionWT - conditionKD`, WT is the test group and KD the
reference (the subtracted term), so the estimate is WT minus KD: positive when a
transcript is used more in WT, negative when it is used more in KD. This
reverses the usual way of describing a knockdown ("KD vs control"), so that the
up side is the condition with PCBP1 present. splicelogic treats the down
(negative-estimate) transcripts as the reference, so every event describes what
WT transcripts do compared with KD ones, as in the RBP workflow. With `~ 0 + condition` there is no intercept, so
the level order (`levels = c("KD", "WT")`) does not change the fit: the
contrast alone sets the direction.

| Event | What happens | What it suggests about PCBP1 |
|---|---|---|
| IE | Exon is in WT transcripts and lost after KD | PCBP1 promotes inclusion |

PCBP1 binding upstream of an exon typically promotes its inclusion, and
knockdown lowers it, so that pattern shows up as IE events, which the analyses
below focus on.

```{r preprare_exons}
# prepare exons for splicelogic
sig_exons <- prepare_exons(
  txdb, sig_res_kd, coef_col = "estimates", verbose = TRUE
)
```

```{r find_events}
#find ie
ie_events <- sig_exons |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates") |> find_ie()

#find all events
events <- sig_exons |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates")|> find_all_events()
```

```{r collapse_redundant_events}
# define a helper function
my_paste <- \(x) paste(unique(x), collapse = ",")
# rows are collapsed when they share the same exon and the same event type. The
# exon is identified by `exon_key` (gene, chromosome, start, end and strand),
# built as in the vignette's recipe for an exon id, rather than by `exon_id`:
# the annotation gives the same exon more than one id when it is coding in one
# transcript and non-coding in another
collapsed_events <- events |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )
```

```{r unfold_kd, include=FALSE}
# from the event counts on, the code is shown
knitr::opts_chunk$set(class.source = NULL)
```

```{r barplot_event_types}
event_counts <- events |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

collapsed_event_counts <- collapsed_events |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

# combine both count tables into one, labelled by source
counts <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "All events" = event_counts,
  "Collapsed events" = collapsed_event_counts,
  .id = "set"
)

# event types from most to fewest events
counts$event_type <- factor(
  counts$event_type,
  levels = event_counts$event_type[order(-event_counts$count)]
)

ggplot(counts, aes(x = event_type, y = count, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "All events" = "#B0CFFF",       # light blue
    "Collapsed events" = "#3A86FF"  # darker blue
  )) +
  labs(title = "Splice event counts",
  x = "Event Type", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r plot_events_by_gene}
# use splicelogic's built-in plotting function to visualize events for a specific gene:
# the one with the most IE events
gene_of_interest <- names(sort(table(ie_events$gene_id), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
# filter events for the gene of interest
events_for_gene <- events[events$gene_id == gene_of_interest]

# visualize the events for the gene of interest
splicelogic::plot_transcripts(events_for_gene, sig_exons, rescale_introns = FALSE) +
  ggtitle(paste("Splice events for gene:", gene_of_interest))
```

```{r save_events_plots, eval=FALSE}
# make a plot for each gene with events and save to files
# plot_transcripts_by_gene returns a list of ggplot objects, one for each gene
plots <- plot_transcripts_by_gene(events, sig_exons)
# save each plot to the same pdf file
pdf(here("workflows/figures/PCBP1_splice_events_by_gene.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
for (gene in names(plots)) {
    print(plots[[gene]])
}
dev.off()
```

## Collapse redundant events

`find_ie()` returns an exon once per transcript pair it is part of: an exon in
two up transcripts and skipped by two down ones comes back four times. The event counts above already collapse these (`collapsed_events`). For
the sequence analyses below we also keep one row per exon, so that an exon
shared by many transcripts does not weigh more in the profiles and logos, and
the background set is sized by exons rather than pairs. `n` records how many
pairs each exon came from. The collapse is the same as in
`collapse_redundant_events`, applied to the IE events, and like it
collapses rows only for the same exon (gene, chromosome, start, end, strand)
and the same event type. Set `collapse_exons <- FALSE` to run the sequence
analyses on every event instead, as before the collapse; the collapsed set
stays available as `ie_collapsed`.

```{r collapse_ie}
# TRUE: the sequence analyses below use one row per exon. FALSE: they use every
# IE event, one row per transcript pair, as before the collapse, to
# compare
collapse_exons <- TRUE

ie_collapsed <- ie_events |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        gene_id = my_paste(gene_id),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )

data.frame(
  events = length(ie_events),
  exons  = length(ie_collapsed),
  max_n  = max(ie_collapsed$n)
)

# the set the sequence analyses below use
ie_exons <- if (collapse_exons) ie_collapsed else ie_events
```

### IE exons per gene

How the IE events spread across genes: the number of distinct IE exons in each
gene. `ie_collapsed` already has one row per exon and gene, with `n` the events
it came from, so the counts come straight from it.

```{r ie_exons_per_gene, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
ie_per_gene <- ie_collapsed |>
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_events = sum(n),
                   n_exons  = plyranges::n())

data.frame(
  ie_events = length(ie_events),
  ie_exons  = length(ie_collapsed),
  ie_genes  = nrow(ie_per_gene)
)

# ggplot needs a data.frame, so the small per-gene summary is converted here
as.data.frame(ie_per_gene) |>
  dplyr::count(n_exons) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(n_exons), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3A86FF", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Distinct IE exons per gene",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d IE events, %d distinct exons, %d genes",
                          length(ie_events), length(ie_collapsed),
                          nrow(ie_per_gene)),
       x = "Distinct IE exons in the gene", y = "Genes") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Sequence context around the event exons, focusing on included exons (IE)

IE exons are the set analysed here (see *Direction of the events* above).

The analysis below uses a set of sequence-context helpers consolidated in
`helper.R` (nucleotide-composition profiles, background exon sampling,
splice-site logos and RBP motif scanning). The splicelogic package itself only
exports `get_seq()` for sequence work, so these stay as paper-repo helpers (for now).

```{r seq_context_helpers, message=FALSE}
source(here("workflows/helper.R"))
```

`slEventFlankProfiles()` takes a finder's output straight away: it flanks each
exon (strand-aware, so "upstream" is 5' in transcription order), slides
overlapping windows across the flank, and returns the per-window nucleotide
fractions for each side.

```{r flank_windows_ie, message=FALSE}
ie_profiles <- slEventFlankProfiles(ie_exons, genome = "hg38", width = 100)

# rows = exons, cols = window_nucleotide (e.g. w1_A)
dim(ie_profiles$upstream)
dim(ie_profiles$downstream)
```


### Background set

We want to compare the sequence context of the events with that of a control set.
For the control set (non-event exons), we sample as many exons as there are in
`ie_exons` (one per IE exon, or one per IE event with `collapse_exons = FALSE`),
drawn at random from the internal exons of transcripts with no evidence of
differential usage (`pval > 0.5`).

```{r non_event_exons}
dtu_res_kd <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/PCBP1/dtu_res_kd.rds"))
non_event <- slSampleNonEventExons(
  dtu_res_kd, exons, n = ie_exons, pval_min = 0.5, seed = 1
)
non_event
```

```{r flank_windows_non_event, message=FALSE}
non_event_profiles <- slEventFlankProfiles(
  non_event, genome = "hg38", width = 100
)
dim(non_event_profiles$upstream)
```

The IE profiles stacked over the non-IE ones, on the same axes:

```{r plot_updownstream_ie, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  slPlotFlankProfiles(ie_profiles, exon_label = "IE"),
  slPlotFlankProfiles(non_event_profiles, exon_label = "non-IE"),
  ncol = 1
)
```

The IE and non-IE sets, one panel per nucleotide (mean ± standard error), and
next to them the difference between them, IE minus non-IE:

```{r plot_ie_vs_non_event, fig.width=14, fig.height=5.5}
ie_vs_non_event <- list(IE = ie_profiles, "non-IE" = non_event_profiles)

patchwork::wrap_plots(
  slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(ie_vs_non_event),
  slPlotFlankProfilesByNt(ie_vs_non_event, difference = TRUE),
  nrow = 1
)
```

An alternative, within-transcript control: for each event, the internal exon of
the same transcript that is shared with the event partner and closest in rank
to the event exon.

```{r matched_non_event_exons, eval=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
matched <- slMatchedNonEventExons(ie_events, exons)

slEventFlankProfiles(matched, genome = "hg38", width = 100) |>
  slPlotFlankProfiles(exon_label = "matched exon")
```

## Splice-site sequence logos

The window profiles above average over 10 bp, which smooths the splice site
away. `slFlankLogoMatrices()` keeps every base position separate and returns a
position frequency matrix per side, running `width` bases into the intron and
`exon_bases` into the exon so the boundary is inside the matrix.

Note which site each side carries: the region **upstream** of an exon is the
end of the preceding intron and holds the **3' splice site** (acceptor,
`...ag | EXON`); the region **downstream** is the start of the following intron
and holds the **5' splice site** (donor, `EXON | gu...`).

```{r logo_events_bits, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3.2}
ie_logo <- slFlankLogoMatrices(ie_exons, genome = "hg38",
                               width = 25, exon_bases = 3)

# letter height = information content, the classic logo scaling: unconstrained
# positions shrink to nothing and the consensus stands out
slPlotFlankLogo(ie_logo, method = "bits")
```

The same for the background set, to see whether the event splice sites differ
from those of exons in transcripts with no differential usage.

```{r logo_non_event, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=13, fig.height=3.2}
non_event_logo <- slFlankLogoMatrices(non_event, genome = "hg38",
                                      width = 25, exon_bases = 3)

slPlotFlankLogo(non_event_logo, method = "bits")
```

```{r logo_difference}
# where the two sets differ most, per position and nucleotide; upstream holds
# the 3' splice site, where a C-rich tract preceding the exon would sit
delta_up <- ie_logo$upstream - non_event_logo$upstream
round(delta_up[, order(-apply(abs(delta_up), 2, max))[1:6]], 3)

delta_down <- ie_logo$downstream - non_event_logo$downstream
round(delta_down[, order(-apply(abs(delta_down), 2, max))[1:6]], 3)
```

## Genes with IE events

Which genes carry the IE exons, how many of them are core essential genes, and
a small GO enrichment. The GO background is every gene tested for DTU
(`dtu_res_kd`): only multi-isoform genes expressed here could have produced an
event, so the whole genome would be the wrong reference.

```{r ie_genes, message=FALSE}
library(org.Hs.eg.db)

# GENCODE ids carry a version suffix; org.Hs.eg.db keys do not
strip_version <- \(x) sub("\\.\\d+$", "", x)

ie_genes <- ie_events |>
  as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_events = dplyr::n(),
                   n_exons  = dplyr::n_distinct(exon_id)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ensembl = strip_version(gene_id),
    symbol  = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, ensembl,
                                    "SYMBOL", "ENSEMBL"),
    entrez  = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, ensembl,
                                    "ENTREZID", "ENSEMBL")
  )

universe <- unique(strip_version(dtu_res_kd$gene_id))
```

Essential genes are taken from the core essential gene list CEGv2 (Hart et
al. 2017, *G3*): 684 genes required for fitness across CRISPR screens in many
cell lines.

```{r ie_genes_essential, message=FALSE}
ceg_file <- here("workflows/data/CEGv2.txt")
if (!file.exists(ceg_file)) {
  download.file(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hart-lab/bagel/master/CEGv2.txt",
    ceg_file
  )
}
ceg <- read.delim(ceg_file, colClasses = "character")

ie_genes$essential <- ie_genes$entrez %in% ceg$ENTREZ_ID

data.frame(
  ie_events        = length(ie_events),
  ie_genes         = nrow(ie_genes),
  with_symbol      = sum(!is.na(ie_genes$symbol)),
  essential        = sum(ie_genes$essential),
  genes_tested_dtu = length(universe)
)

# the 20 IE genes with the most events (`ie_genes` has them all)
ie_genes |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_events), symbol) |>
  dplyr::select(symbol, gene_id, n_events, n_exons, essential) |>
  head(20)
```

```{r plot_ie_genes_essential_only, fig.width=7, fig.height=2}
# share of the IE genes that are core essential
ie_essential_df <- data.frame(
  set    = sprintf("IE genes\n(n = %s)", scales::comma(nrow(ie_genes))),
  status = factor(c("essential", "not essential"),
                  levels = c("essential", "not essential")),
  n      = c(sum(ie_genes$essential), sum(!ie_genes$essential))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(frac  = n / sum(n),
                label = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", scales::comma(n), 100 * frac))

ggplot(ie_essential_df, aes(x = frac, y = set, fill = status)) +
  geom_col(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = \(d) dplyr::filter(d, status == "essential"),
            aes(label = label), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.01,
            size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = \(d) dplyr::filter(d, status == "not essential"),
            aes(x = 0.99, label = label), hjust = 1,
            size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("essential"     = "#3A86FF",
                               "not essential" = "grey85")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(title = "Core essential genes (CEGv2) among IE genes",
       x = "Share of genes", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        plot.margin = margin(5.5, 14, 5.5, 5.5))
```

```{r ie_genes_go, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
# GO biological process; cutoffs at 1 so the top terms are always shown, but
# with ~50 genes few will pass p.adjust < 0.05, so read p.adjust first
ie_go <- clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene     = ie_genes$ensembl,
  universe = universe,
  OrgDb    = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType  = "ENSEMBL",
  ont      = "BP",
  pvalueCutoff = 1,
  qvalueCutoff = 1,
  readable = TRUE
)

as_tibble(ie_go) |>
  dplyr::select(Description, GeneRatio, BgRatio, pvalue, p.adjust, geneID) |>
  head(10)

enrichplot::dotplot(ie_go, showCategory = 10) +
  labs(title = "GO biological process, IE genes",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d term(s) at p.adjust < 0.05",
                          sum(ie_go@result$p.adjust < 0.05)))
```

# Iron chelation (GSE279949)

The same analysis for the iron chelation series. Objects from this comparison
carry a `_chel` suffix, so they do not overwrite the knockdown ones above.

## DTU testing with satuRn: iron chelation (GSE279949)

Same steps, comparing the iron chelator (`CHEL`) against DMSO (`DMSO`).

```{r fold_chel, include=FALSE}
# fold the code of the chelation setup chunks, up to its event counts
knitr::opts_chunk$set(class.source = "fold-hide")
```

```{r filter_chel}
se_chel <- se[, se$experiment == "chelator"]
dim(se_chel)

# counts >= 10 in at least 3 samples (the size of one group)
keep <- rowSums(assay(se_chel) >= 10) >= 3
se_chel <- se_chel[keep, ]
dim(se_chel)
```

```{r dtu_design_chel}
# DMSO as reference level
colData(se_chel)$condition <- factor(colData(se_chel)$condition, levels = c("DMSO", "CHEL"))

# build design from the factor directly (matches satuRn vignette convention)
condition <- colData(se_chel)$condition
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition)

L <- limma::makeContrasts(
  CHEL_vs_DMSO = conditionCHEL - conditionDMSO,
  levels = design
)
L
```

```{r dtu_fit_chel, message=FALSE}
rowData(se_chel)$isoform_id <- rowData(se_chel)$tx_name
# flatten CharacterList gene_id to plain character
rowData(se_chel)$gene_id <- vapply(rowData(se_chel)$gene_id, `[`, character(1), 1)

se_chel <- se_chel[
  duplicated(rowData(se_chel)$gene_id) |
    duplicated(rowData(se_chel)$gene_id, fromLast = TRUE),
]
dim(se_chel)
se_chel <- satuRn::fitDTU(se_chel, formula = ~0 + condition)
```

```{r dtu_test_chel, message=FALSE}
se_chel <- satuRn::testDTU(
  object = se_chel,
  contrasts = L,
  diagplot1 = TRUE,
  diagplot2 = TRUE
)
```

```{r dtu_results_chel}
gene_ids <- rowData(se_chel)$gene_id

dtu_res_chel <- rowData(se_chel)[["fitDTUResult_CHEL_vs_DMSO"]] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("tx_name") |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(gene_id = gene_ids) |>
  dplyr::select(tx_name, gene_id, estimates, pval, regular_FDR) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pval)

sig_res_chel <- dtu_res_chel |> dplyr::filter(regular_FDR < 0.1)

sig_res_chel <- sig_res_chel |> mutate(tx_id = tx_name)
sig_res_chel
# save for later use
saveRDS(dtu_res_chel, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/dtu_res_chel.rds"))
saveRDS(sig_res_chel, here("workflows/data/PCBP1/sig_res_chel.rds"))
```

```{r load_sig_res_chel}
# load the saved DTU results
sig_res_chel <- readRDS(here("workflows/data/PCBP1/sig_res_chel.rds"))
sig_res_chel
```

## Splice event detection with splicelogic for iron chelation

We run event detection on the iron chelation comparison (`sig_res_chel`). Both
comparisons use the same FDR cut-off (`regular_FDR < 0.1`), so their event
counts can be compared; chelation still has about ten times more significant
transcripts than the knockdown.

### Direction of the events

CHEL (iron chelated) is the up side and DMSO (iron present) the reference. In
the contrast `CHEL_vs_DMSO = conditionCHEL - conditionDMSO`, CHEL is the test
group and DMSO the reference (the subtracted term), so the estimate is CHEL
minus DMSO: positive when a transcript is used more after chelation, negative
when it is used more in DMSO. Every event describes what chelated transcripts do
compared with DMSO ones. As for the
knockdown, the level order (`levels = c("DMSO", "CHEL")`) does not change the
fit: the contrast alone sets the direction.

CHEL is the up side because PCBP1 is expected to act more in low iron, so in
both comparisons the up side is the condition with more PCBP1 activity (WT for
the knockdown, CHEL here). IE events then mean the same thing in both, exons
whose inclusion PCBP1 promotes, which is why the analyses below focus on IE as
in the knockdown section.


| Event | What happens | What it suggests about low iron |
|---|---|---|
| IE | Exon is in chelated transcripts and absent from DMSO ones | Low iron promotes inclusion |

```{r preprare_exons_chel}
# prepare exons for splicelogic
sig_exons_chel <- prepare_exons(
  txdb, sig_res_chel, coef_col = "estimates", verbose = TRUE
)
```

```{r find_events_chel}
#find ie
ie_events_chel <- sig_exons_chel |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates") |> find_ie()

#find all events
events_chel <- sig_exons_chel |> preprocess(coef_col = "estimates") |> find_all_events()
```

```{r collapse_redundant_events_chel}
# my_paste() is defined in the knockdown section
collapsed_events_chel <- events_chel |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )
```

```{r unfold_chel, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(class.source = NULL)
```

```{r barplot_event_types_chel}
event_counts_chel <- events_chel |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

collapsed_event_counts_chel <- collapsed_events_chel |>
    as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::group_by(event_type) |>
    dplyr::summarise(count = dplyr::n())

# combine both count tables into one, labelled by source
counts_chel <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  "All events" = event_counts_chel,
  "Collapsed events" = collapsed_event_counts_chel,
  .id = "set"
)

# event types from most to fewest events
counts_chel$event_type <- factor(
  counts_chel$event_type,
  levels = event_counts_chel$event_type[order(-event_counts_chel$count)]
)

ggplot(counts_chel, aes(x = event_type, y = count, fill = set)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "All events" = "#B0CFFF",       # light blue
    "Collapsed events" = "#3A86FF"  # darker blue
  )) +
  labs(title = "Splice event counts, iron chelation",
  x = "Event Type", y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r plot_events_by_gene_chel}
# use splicelogic's built-in plotting function to visualize events for a specific gene:
# the one with the most IE events
gene_of_interest_chel <- names(sort(table(ie_events_chel$gene_id), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
# filter events for the gene of interest
events_for_gene_chel <- events_chel[events_chel$gene_id == gene_of_interest_chel]

# visualize the events for the gene of interest
splicelogic::plot_transcripts(events_for_gene_chel, sig_exons_chel, rescale_introns = FALSE) +
  ggtitle(paste("Splice events for gene:", gene_of_interest_chel))
```

```{r save_events_plots_chel, eval=FALSE}
# make a plot for each gene with events and save to files
# plot_transcripts_by_gene returns a list of ggplot objects, one for each gene
plots_chel <- plot_transcripts_by_gene(events_chel, sig_exons_chel)
# save each plot to the same pdf file
pdf(here("workflows/figures/PCBP1_chel_splice_events_by_gene.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
for (gene in names(plots_chel)) {
    print(plots_chel[[gene]])
}
dev.off()
```

## Collapse redundant events

As for the knockdown: one row per exon for the sequence analyses below, with
`n` the number of transcript pairs each exon came from, collapsing rows
only for the same exon (gene, chromosome, start, end, strand) and event type.
`collapse_exons_chel <- FALSE` runs the sequence analyses on every event
instead.

```{r collapse_ie_chel}
# TRUE: the sequence analyses below use one row per exon. FALSE: they use every
# IE event, one row per transcript pair, as before the collapse, to
# compare
collapse_exons_chel <- TRUE

ie_collapsed_chel <- ie_events_chel |>
    dplyr::mutate(exon_key = paste(gene_id, seqnames, start, end, strand, sep = ":")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(exon_key, event_type) |>
    plyranges::reduce_ranges_directed(
        n = plyranges::n(),
        gene_id = my_paste(gene_id),
        exon_id = my_paste(exon_id),
        tx_id = my_paste(tx_id),
        exon_rank = my_paste(exon_rank),
        event_tx_id = my_paste(event_tx_id),
  )

data.frame(
  events = length(ie_events_chel),
  exons  = length(ie_collapsed_chel),
  max_n  = max(ie_collapsed_chel$n)
)

# the set the sequence analyses below use
ie_exons_chel <- if (collapse_exons_chel) ie_collapsed_chel else ie_events_chel
```

### IE exons per gene

How the IE events spread across genes: the number of distinct IE exons in each
gene. `ie_collapsed_chel` already has one row per exon and gene, with `n` the events

```{r ie_exons_per_gene_chel, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
ie_per_gene_chel <- ie_collapsed_chel |>
  dplyr::group_by(gene_id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_events = sum(n),

data.frame(

  ie_genes  = nrow(ie_per_gene_chel)
)

# ggplot needs a data.frame, so the small per-gene summary is converted here
as.data.frame(ie_per_gene_chel) |>
  dplyr::count(n_exons) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(n_exons), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3A86FF", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Distinct IE exons per gene, iron chelation",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d IE events, %d distinct exons, %d genes",
                          length(ie_events_chel), length(ie_collapsed_chel),
                          nrow(ie_per_gene_chel)),
```


# Knockdown vs chelation

## IE events in both comparisons

In both comparisons the up side is the condition with more PCBP1 activity (WT
for the knockdown, CHEL for the chelation), so an IE event means the same thing
in both: an exon whose inclusion goes with more PCBP1 activity. If chelation
acts through PCBP1, the IE events of the two comparisons should overlap.

The overlap is counted at three levels: genes, transcripts (only those that
include the IE exon, `tx_id`, not the partner transcripts that skip it) and
exons (`exon_key`, the gene and exact position, from the collapsed sets). Both
comparisons use the same annotation (GENCODE v43), so the identifiers match.
Chelation has many more IE events than the knockdown, so the telling number is
the share of the knockdown set that is also found after chelation
(`kd_in_chel`).

```{r ie_overlap}
ie_sets <- list(
  genes = list(
    kd   = unique(ie_events$gene_id),
    chel = unique(ie_events_chel$gene_id)
  ),
  transcripts = list(
    kd   = unique(ie_events$tx_id),
    chel = unique(ie_events_chel$tx_id)
  ),
  exons = list(
    kd   = unique(ie_collapsed$exon_key),
    chel = unique(ie_collapsed_chel$exon_key)
  )
)

ie_overlap <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ie_sets), function(level) {
  kd     <- ie_sets[[level]]$kd
  chel   <- ie_sets[[level]]$chel
  shared <- intersect(kd, chel)
  data.frame(
    level      = level,
    knockdown  = length(kd),
    chelation  = length(chel),
    shared     = length(shared),
    kd_in_chel = round(length(shared) / length(kd), 3),
    chel_in_kd = round(length(shared) / length(chel), 3),
    jaccard    = round(length(shared) / length(union(kd, chel)), 3)
  )
}))
ie_overlap
```

UpSet plots for genes and transcripts: the bars on top are the knockdown-only,
shared and chelation-only sets, the dots below show which comparison each bar
belongs to, and the bars on the left are the size of each IE set. The shared set
is highlighted.

```{r plot_ie_overlap, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5, out.width="50%", fig.show="hold", warning=FALSE}
# one UpSet plot per level; out.width = 50% puts the two side by side
for (level in c("genes", "transcripts")) {
  print(UpSetR::upset(
    UpSetR::fromList(list(Knockdown = ie_sets[[level]]$kd,
                          Chelation = ie_sets[[level]]$chel)),
    sets            = c("Chelation", "Knockdown"),
    keep.order      = TRUE,
    order.by        = "freq",
    main.bar.color  = "grey40",
    sets.bar.color  = "grey40",
    queries         = list(list(query  = UpSetR::intersects,
                                params = list("Knockdown", "Chelation"),
                                color  = "#3A86FF", active = TRUE)),
    mainbar.y.label = paste("IE", level),
    sets.x.label    = "IE set size",
    text.scale      = 1.3
  ))
  grid::grid.text(paste("IE", level), x = 0.02, y = 0.98,
                  just = c("left", "top"),
                  gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 14, fontface = "bold"))
}
```

The genes and transcripts with IE events in both comparisons: the shared genes
with their full name and number of IE events in each comparison, and the
transcripts that include an IE exon in both.

```{r ie_overlap_names}
shared_genes <- intersect(ie_sets$genes$kd, ie_sets$genes$chel)

ie_genes |>
  dplyr::filter(gene_id %in% shared_genes) |>
  dplyr::select(symbol, gene_id, n_events_kd = n_events) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::select(ie_genes_chel, gene_id, n_events_chel = n_events),
    by = "gene_id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    name = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, strip_version(gene_id),
                                 "GENENAME", "ENSEMBL"),
    .after = gene_id
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(symbol) |>
  knitr::kable()

tibble::tibble(
  tx_id = intersect(ie_sets$transcripts$kd, ie_sets$transcripts$chel)
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    dplyr::distinct(tibble::tibble(tx_id   = ie_events$tx_id,
                                   gene_id = ie_events$gene_id)),
    by = "tx_id"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(ie_genes, gene_id, symbol), by = "gene_id") |>
  dplyr::select(symbol, gene_id, tx_id) |>
  dplyr::arrange(symbol, tx_id) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

GO annotation of the shared genes, from org.Hs.eg.db with the term names from
GO.db: one row per gene and ontology (BP biological process, MF molecular
function, CC cellular component).

```{r ie_overlap_go, message=FALSE}
shared_go <- AnnotationDbi::select(
  org.Hs.eg.db, keys = strip_version(shared_genes),
  columns = c("SYMBOL", "GO", "ONTOLOGY"), keytype = "ENSEMBL"
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(GO)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(SYMBOL, GO, ONTOLOGY)

go_terms <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(GO.db::GO.db, unique(shared_go$GO),
                                  "TERM", "GOID")
shared_go$term <- go_terms[shared_go$GO]

shared_go |>
  dplyr::mutate(ONTOLOGY = factor(ONTOLOGY, levels = c("BP", "MF", "CC"))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(symbol = SYMBOL, ontology = ONTOLOGY) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_terms = dplyr::n_distinct(term),
                   terms   = paste(sort(unique(term)), collapse = "; "),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(symbol, ontology) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
